gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Tektur draws pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin anywhere. Noto Sans Marchen brings small letters that stand almost as tall as capitals, their curves ending in clear daylight.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Tektur gives its stems and crossbars one thickness, and every curve opens up with a generous gap at the end. Noto Sans Mende Kikakui lets daylight through every bowl, its lowercase towering.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundari: Noto Sans Nag Mundari unwraps its curves halfway, with lowercase that rivals the capitals. Noto Sans Nag Mundari keeps a long paragraph moving, while Tektur traces its glyphs in one thickness above.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Expressive Tektur draws every line as if with ruler and compass, its curves generously open. Noto Sans Ogham sits beneath with tall bodies that look bold, and wide gaps in the e.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Small text stays legible, with large open counters in the tall a, e and s. Noto Sans Old Hungarian is the sans under Tektur, whose letters look bent from a single length of wire.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ara: Tektur has a tube-like stroke that resembles neon glass, with generous openings on every curve. Noto Sans Old North Arabian is a sans-serif whose dense, tall lowercase band keeps paragraphs compact and steady.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Tektur never lets its curves thin out at the turns. That makes it the louder voice, while Noto Sans Old Permic quietly handles the reading with rounded forms open to the side.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Tektur runs a single flat line weight through every glyph, with lowercase built oversized. Noto Sans Old Persian lets its open counters breathe into the white space, so paragraphs feel lofty and light.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Tektur has a blueprint-lettering feel, its constant line running through every oversized lowercase letter. And Noto Sans Old Sogdian stays crisp when shrunk, its wide-mouthed letters rising nearly to cap height.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Tektur keeps its stroke ends as wide as the middle. Noto Sans Oriya, a sans with generous curve gaps, reads smoothly as its small letters nearly reach the capitals.
